documents.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
documents.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
documents.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. documents.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. documents.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
documents.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin

documents.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
documents.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. documents.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
documents.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. documents.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
documents.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. documents.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
documents.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. documents.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
documents.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionali

documents.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
documents.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
documents.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

documents.title: Multiscale computational modeling of circulating tumor cells: From separation and detection to targeted drug delivery.
documents.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) provide a minimally invasive window into cancer progression and metastatic dissemination; however, their extreme rarity, phenotypic heterogeneity, and mechanical adaptability make their isolation, identification, and therapeutic targeting challenging. Although computational methods have been applied to individual steps of CTC research, the field lacks a unified framework connecting molecular recognition, cell mechanics, microfluidic separation, detection, vascular transport, and targeted drug delivery. This review addresses that gap by organizing computational ap

documents.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
documents.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. documents.title: In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.
documents.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major public health threat in Africa and South America. Although the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective, its use is restricted in certain vulnerable populations, emphasizing the need for nonreplicating alternatives. We performed an integrated in silico characterization of two production-optimized recombinant YFV envelope (Env) proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains. Physicochemical, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), electrostatic, and immune sim

documents.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.
documents.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted
documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.
documents.abstract: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B

documents.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
documents.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing

documents.title: Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.
documents.abstract: PFAS coatings impart strong water and oil repellency on materials, but their environmental persistence necessitates sustainable alternatives. The development of alternative chemistries is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic water and oil wettability. Here, a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulation framework was developed to predict and rationalize the intrinsic water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon for both water and oil. By systematically sampling PFAS head group types (-CHO, -COOH,

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.
documents.abstract: Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. documents.title: Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.
documents.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling "photonic substituent effects." Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. documents.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
documents.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.

documents.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
documents.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. documents.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
documents.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).

documents.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
documents.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language

documents.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
documents.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. documents.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
documents.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent

documents.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer under exposure to synthetic phenolic antioxidants: An integrated network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
documents.abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM

documents.title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study.
documents.abstract: Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
